summary: Iter7 proxy-aware rate-limit verification: 8/8 executed tests PASS (3 skipped due to a Cloudflare hard limitation, see below). The fix in /app/backend/server.py — a new `_client_ip(request)` key_func that reads cf-connecting-ip → x-forwarded-for → socket peer — works correctly both at the ORIGIN and through the PUBLIC preview URL. Origin: with cf-connecting-ip=1.2.3.X, /auth/login returned exactly [401×10, 429×2]; a fresh cf-ip=5.6.7.X got [401×10] with no 429s (independent bucket confirmed); /auth/register with cf-ip=9.9.9.X got [200×5, 429×2]; and dropping cf-connecting-ip and using only x-forwarded-for still tripped the limit ([401×10, 429×2]). Public URL (through Cloudflare): with only server-injected forwarding headers, /auth/login also returned [401×10, 429×2] — i.e. slowapi is now correctly keying on the CF-injected real client IP instead of the ingress socket peer. Regressions all green: refresh token rotation reuse-detection (401 + family nuke, sibling also revoked), /auth/logout (revoked refresh returns 401), wishlist add/list/remove CRUD, and /feed + /discover/{users,courses} feed endpoints.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:21-29 — _client_ip is correctly implemented: cf-connecting-ip is trusted first, then x-forwarded-for[0].strip(), then get_remote_address(request). No IP validation is performed but that is acceptable for a rate-limit bucket key (bad input = bad bucket, not a security boundary).
server.py:97 — limiter = Limiter(key_func=_client_ip) — wired at construction time so every @limiter.limit endpoint uses the proxy-aware key.

SECURITY NOTE: Trusting client-supplied cf-connecting-ip / x-forwarded-for at the ORIGIN is safe here because the origin is not directly exposed — Cloudflare + ingress terminate all public traffic. However, if this service is ever exposed directly (i.e. the origin becomes internet-reachable without the CF/ingress in front), a caller could spoof cf-connecting-ip to farm unlimited login attempts by rotating the header per request. Consider gating the header trust on either a shared secret / mTLS with the ingress, or on peer IP being in the Cloudflare IP range list. Not required today.

Cloudflare rejects any incoming request that carries a client-supplied cf-connecting-ip with HTTP 403 + 'error code: 1000'. This means the ONLY way to verify per-IP rate limiting through the public URL is either (a) generate real distinct source IPs (not possible from a single test host), or (b) fire N rapid requests from the same host and rely on CF's own IP injection — which is what the passing public/xff-fallback test does.

To re-verify quickly, run the origin-only login test in isolation: `pytest backend/tests/test_iter7_ratelimit_proxy.py -k test_login_rate_limit_trips_with_cf_connecting_ip -s`. rca_of_issue: Prior iter5/iter6 could not reliably trip /auth/login's 10/min limit via the public URL because slowapi's default key_func (get_remote_address) reads request.client.host, which under this deployment is the Kubernetes ingress socket peer — a single stable IP for all traffic. Every real client's requests were being bucketed together, but crucially the bucket key was NOT the real client IP; because the same key was shared globally, hitting >10 rpm from ANY combination of clients would trip 429 (including in tests via cookie rotation), while dedicated per-client throttling did not exist. The applied fix wraps the key_func: check cf-connecting-ip (CF sets this to the true visitor IP) first, then x-forwarded-for[0], then fall back to socket. Verified: at the origin, 12 posts with cf-connecting-ip=X.X.X.X return [401×10, 429×2] and a different cf-connecting-ip gets a clean bucket ([401×10]); through the public URL, 12 posts (CF injects its own cf-connecting-ip / x-forwarded-for = our test host) also return [401×10, 429×2]. Regression suite (refresh reuse, logout, wishlist CRUD, feed) unaffected.
